findings.evidence: Balance between documenting for future-you and showcasing for others.

findings.evidence: A project meant for public release with no license chosen yet is OSS with a License placeholder.
findings.fix: Add a Gotchas bullet: a missing license is not an assumed OSI license. Publishing the README as if MIT or Apache-2.0 applied makes a legal claim the repository does not support; keep the License placeholder and name the SPDX id only after LICENSE or the manifest has one.

findings.evidence: `templates/personal.md`: only when the type is Personal.
findings.fix: Give personal.md the same conditional content the other templates get: load it for a side project or portfolio piece, keep "What I learned" only when the user wants portfolio reflection, and say "personal project" instead of inventing a license.

findings.evidence: then give the full README (creating), the changed sections or a diff (updating)
findings.fix: Default to the full README when creating and to a diff of the changed sections when updating; use pasted changed sections only when the user asks not to edit the file.

findings.evidence: "Does not fabricate a specific license or repository facts not supplied"
findings.fix: Add an assertion that the draft leaves the license as a visible placeholder when none is supplied, and a second eval whose prompt names a published package version plus a default-branch-only API so the expected output marks that example unreleased.

findings.evidence: "query":"Create a README for my new open-source Python package with install and usage examples."
findings.fix: Replace two explicit should-trigger queries with prompts that never say README, such as a monorepo package whose copied install steps 404 and a dotfiles directory future-you cannot navigate, and add a near-miss negative that asks to fix the same claims inside docs/getting-started.md rather than README.md.

findings.evidence: No official PyPI or Python Packaging User Guide page states this relative-link behavior (checked 2026-11-15 at https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/making-a-pypi-friendly-readme/, which does not address it), so verify the current PyPI rendering before applying this rule.
findings.fix: Resolve the branch in the same bullet: keep absolute, tag-pinned URLs as the default for any README that ships on PyPI, and change one to a relative link only after a live project-page check shows that relative link resolving.
